entry.focal: A 3 m tall orange-brown wall (the tsuboniwa proxy) filling the left two-thirds of the frame, with a 1.05 m glowing lantern block in front.
entry.next_visible: No. The hero box blocks the hall; nothing beyond is visible.

reveal.focal: Same orange wall at close range, with a bench and a glowing lantern block in the foreground.
reveal.next_visible: The engawa running east on the left, dim grey room boxes.

concept.focal: Vanishing point down the engawa: grey room boxes left, the orange garden wall right, small lantern blocks. The perspective works, but nothing glows like shoji.
concept.next_visible: End of the hall is dark; the north passage is not readable.

strip.focal: Walls and lantern blocks. strip-7 shows the teal corridor through the north door, a good glimpse but cool rather than warm.
strip.next_visible: Yes at the end (cor_east's teal water through the north door).

fixes.detail: tsuboniwa is an opaque 9x6.5x3 m box, so the 'small lit courtyard' reads as a solid wall that blocks both thresholds' sightlines. Replace the proxy with a sunken open court: a 0.3 m kerb, floor at -20.3, one 3 m pine, a stone toro, and an emissive washi light box (about 6x4 m) at the ceiling (-16.2) as the brightest thing in the hall.

Rooms are blank grey boxes. Their 80 W area light doesn't show. Make the engawa-facing front an emissive washi/shoji panel (warm, low) with one dark post every 1.8 m so the hall gets 'shoji glowing left and right' and dark gaps between rooms.

Nine 1.05 m fully emissive lantern_floor blocks are the brightest objects in every frame and spread evenly on both sides. Cut to 5 low andon (h ~0.6, 15 W), one per room door, alternating sides. Remove lights0:5 (125.9,63.17) and lights0:0 (122.85,64.7), which bracket an empty foyer, and lights0:6 (126.94,69.37), which sits in front of the bench and blocks the reveal.

Gravel-strip stones sit at z -20.25 with h 0.3, so they read as flat tiles on the floor. Seat them at -20.05 (or drop them). The density problem is elsewhere: the hall needs posts, a tokonoma niche or bench groupings at the room doors.
The east-end bonsai at (158.8,72.6) closes the vista. Light it with a small uplight or spot so the engawa has an end-stop instead of a dark wall.

top_change: Turn the garden from a solid 3 m box into an open sunken court under a bright washi light box, so it becomes the calm bright focal point both doors look at.
plausibility: Hero proxy is a 3 m solid block inside a 4 m hall: you couldn't see the garden 'diagonally from both thresholds'.
Gravel stones are sunk flush with the floor.
Hall reads cool grey, not warm hinoki (lighting/material only, but it changes the mood judgement).
